claims.text: Partial cobalt substitution in a Mn-based Heusler alloy can enhance its magnetocaloric properties.
Cobalt substitution will tune magnetic exchange interactions in the Mn-based Heusler alloy.
Cobalt substitution will tune the phase behavior of the Mn-based Heusler alloy.
The proposed initial material is an undoped Mn-based Heusler alloy, such as a Ni-Mn-based alloy.
The proposed intervention is to replace part of the Mn or another magnetic element with approximately 5–10% cobalt.
Magnetocaloric measurements near room temperature under an approximately 2 T magnetic field are relevant to practical magnetic refrigeration.
Cobalt substitution will change the austenite-martensite structural transition.
Modified magnetic exchange interactions will shift the critical temperature closer to room temperature.
Cobalt substitution will produce a more pronounced first-order phase transition.
A more pronounced first-order phase transition will produce a larger isothermal entropy change.
A more pronounced first-order phase transition will improve refrigerant capacity.
The cobalt-doped alloy will have a higher isothermal entropy change than the undoped alloy under identical conditions.
The cobalt-doped alloy will have greater refrigerant capacity than the undoped alloy under identical conditions.
The cobalt-doped alloy's Curie temperature will move toward room temperature.
The magnetocaloric enhancement will depend on the cobalt concentration and overall alloy composition.
Excessive cobalt doping may form secondary phases.
Secondary-phase formation may suppress the beneficial magnetocaloric effect.
